v1.text: 1223. Twenty to thirty thousand riders nobody had ever heard of came over the Caucasus Mountains.

v2.text: Facing them: Rus princes and Cumans. Chroniclers say several times as many.

v2b.text: Leading the Mongols was a veteran general named Subutai.

v3.text: But for days, the Mongols didn't fight. They ran.

v4.text: The allies chased them eagerly, never noticing how far their own column was stretching.

v5.text: Then, at the Kalka River, the Mongols turned around.

v6.text: They cut off the head of the long column, and closed the trap.

v6c.text: The Rus troops far behind could do nothing to help. Fake a defeat, draw the enemy out, then strike the moment their lines break apart.

v6b.text: This was the Mongols' signature move: the feigned retreat.

v7.text: This is how the Mongols conquered so much of the world, and we'll show you every battle. The Mongol invasion of Europe starts now!

v6d.text: Meanwhile, the Mongol wings swung wide to seal off the rear, and horse archers rained arrows from every side. With no way out, the vanguard collapsed.
